numberItems.stem: A small bus is designed for exactly 10 persons, including the driver. Does the "P" endorsement rule apply to it?
options: Yes, because the rule covers 10 or more persons
No, because the rule is more than 10 persons, including the driver
Only if more than 15 persons ride, not counting the driver
numberItems.explanation: The "P" endorsement is needed for a vehicle designed to carry more than 10 persons, including the driver; exactly 10 is not more than 10 (p. 4-1).

numberItems.stem: You pass your skills test in a van built for 15 persons or less, counting the driver. What may you drive?
options: Only a bus for 10 persons or less
Only a 15-passenger-or-less small-size bus
Any size bus, since you now have the "P" endorsement
numberItems.explanation: Testing in a van for 15 persons or less restricts your license to a 15-passenger-or-less small-size bus, because you showed your skill only in a small vehicle (p. 4-1).

numberItems.stem: Your bus has air brakes. Which knowledge test sections must you pass for the "P" endorsement?
options: Sections 2 and 4 only
Sections 2, 4, and 5
Sections 4 and 5 only
numberItems.explanation: You pass written tests on Sections 2 and 4, add the Section 5 air brakes test if the bus has air brakes, then pass the skills tests (p. 4-1).

numberItems.stem: How big is each diamond-shaped HazMat hazard label?
options: 2 inches
4 inches
9 inches
numberItems.explanation: There are 9 different hazard labels, each 4 inches and diamond-shaped; 2 inches is the width of the standee line (pp. 4-2, 4-3).

numberItems.stem: Which of these may a bus NEVER carry?
options: Division 2.3 poison gas
Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D
Emergency hospital supplies
numberItems.explanation: Division 2.3 poison gas, liquid Class 6 poison, tear gas, and irritating material are never allowed; ORM-D small-arms ammunition and emergency hospital supplies may be carried (p. 4-3).

numberItems.stem: A shipper wants to send 120 pounds of solid Class 6 poison on your bus. What is the rule?
options: Allowed, because the total is under 500 pounds
Not allowed: a bus may never carry more than 100 pounds of this kind of poison
Allowed, if the shipper cannot send it any other way
numberItems.explanation: A bus must never carry more than 100 pounds of solid Class 6 poisons; 500 pounds is the separate limit for all allowed HazMat together (p. 4-3).

numberItems.stem: A bus carries 90 pounds of one allowed HazMat class and 90 pounds of another. Is that within the weight limits?
options: No, because the total is over 100 pounds
Yes, because each class is under 100 pounds and the total is under 500 pounds
No, because two classes may never ride together
numberItems.explanation: The limits are no more than 500 pounds total and no more than 100 pounds of any one class; 90 + 90 = 180 pounds meets both (p. 4-3).

numberItems.stem: A bus built to allow standing riders must show where they cannot stand. How?
options: With a 4-inch diamond-shaped sign
With a 2-inch line on the floor, or another way to show it
With a rope across the aisle at the front door
numberItems.explanation: The standee line is a 2-inch line on the floor (or another means); no rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat (p. 4-3).
